candidate_ideas.statement: Define Z:=V(Fitt_1(R^1 pi_* O_C(Gamma))) inside M_{6,6}. Then Z is closed, S_6-stable, formation-compatible with arbitrary base change, equals V(Fitt_2(R^1 pi_*(omega(-Gamma)))), and equals V(I_{k-2}(phi)) for every 2-term complex phi:K^0->K^1 of ranks k,k-1 universally computing R pi_* O_C(Gamma).

A geometric point (C,p_1,...,p_6) lies in Z iff h^0(O_C(Gamma))>=3 iff h^0(omega_C(-Gamma))>=2 iff there exists a degree-4 line bundle D with h^0(D)>=2 and Gamma+D in |omega_C|; for non-hyperelliptic C these hold with equality h^0(O_C(Gamma))=3 and h^0(omega_C(-Gamma))=2, so omega_C(-Gamma) is a g^1_4, equivalently the six canonical images span at most a P^3 in P^5.

Under H1 (O_{P(E^vee)}(1)|_C = omega_C tensor gamma^*O_{P1}(2)) and H2 (F=O(4)+O(5)), for base-point-free degree-4 gamma one has W_4|_C = omega_C^{tensor 2} and W_5|_C = omega_C^{tensor 2}(-D_gamma); H^0(omega_C tensor W_4^vee(Gamma))=0 always; and H^0(omega_C tensor W_5^vee(Gamma)) is nonzero iff O_C(Gamma)=W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1}=omega_C(-D_gamma) iff Gamma+D_gamma is canonical.

Under H1 and H2, the image in M_{6,6} of the balanced CE evaluation-obstruction locus equals the open substack Z^{bal} of Z consisting of points at which omega_C(-Gamma) carries a base-point-free pencil with balanced CE splitting.

A general complete intersection C of bidegrees (1,2) and (2,2) in P^1 x P^2 is smooth, connected, of genus 6, with omega_C=O_C(1,1), pr_1|_C of degree 4, D_gamma=O_C(1,0), omega_C(-D_gamma)=O_C(0,1) base-point-free of degree 6 with h^0=3, CE data E^vee=O(-3)^{+3} and F=O(4)+O(5); a general member of |O_C(0,1)| is six distinct points and yields a point of both Z and Z^{bal}.

Z->M_6 is surjective; over the Petri-general locus the fibre is the disjoint union over the five points of W^2_6(C) of the ordered-distinct-support open of |L|≅P^2, so Z has a dominant component smooth of dimension 17 and of codimension 4 in M_{6,6}.

In the determinantal presentation of Z as {rk phi <= k-3} for ranks k,k-1, the expected codimension is 3*2=6; with actual codimension 4 on the dominant component, Z carries excess dimension 2 relative to that presentation.

Z->[Z/S_6] is a finite etale S_6-torsor of algebraic stacks and [Z/S_6] is the reduced-support open of the relative degree-six effective-divisor incidence stack; the analogous coarse-moduli statement is false because curve automorphisms yield nontrivial stabilizers.

For unbalanced splitting F=O(3)+O(6) the surviving obstruction has degree +4 and defines a strictly larger locus than the degree-zero triviality condition characterizing balanced obstruction; thus Z captures only the balanced CE obstruction.
By Clifford, on non-hyperelliptic genus-6 curves with deg Gamma=6 one has h^0(O_C(Gamma)) in {1,2,3}, with h^0>=4 supported only over the hyperelliptic locus.

invalid_steps.mathematical_reason: Openness and nonemptiness do not imply nonclosedness: an open nonempty subset may still be closed in the ambient space (e.g. a union of connected components), and no point of the closure lying in Z minus Z^{bal}, no degeneration to an unbalanced or base-pointed residual pencil, and no density of the balanced locus is supplied.
invalid_steps.statement: From openness of base-point-freeness/balancedness together with nonemptiness of Z^{bal}, conclude that the balanced image Z^{bal} is not closed in M_{6,6}.

invalid_steps.mathematical_reason: Excess dimension relative to the generic determinantal formula shows only that the generic expected codimension is not attained; a degeneracy locus may still be locally cut out by a regular sequence of its actual codimension. A nowhere-lci conclusion requires local depth, conormal, or regular-sequence calculations at every point, which are not provided by the global expected-versus-actual comparison alone.
invalid_steps.statement: From expected determinantal codimension 6 versus observed codimension 4 on a dominant component, conclude that Z is nowhere cut out by a regular sequence in that presentation (nowhere locally a complete intersection of length 4).
